issue_context.title: add "created_at" to follow_requests API endpoint
issue_context.body:
### Pitch

The `api/v1/follow_requests` endpoint returns a list of accounts, but no information about when the follow request was sent, while the `api/v1/notifications?types[]=["follow_request"]` endpoint returns the date of the follow request, but only of the 30 most recent notifications.

I would appreciate there being some way to get a list of pending follow requests with the time/date the request was made.

### Motivation

This is completely selfish, it's a feature I need. That's the motivation. I'm getting more follow requests than I can go through every day, and I was hoping to automate the process of adding notes to the requesters' profiles containing the date they requested and why.
comments: Hi! This may be a bit tricky because we currently return accounts rather than follow request objects. That being said, there is precedent to adding fields to `Account` entities on API requests, with `/api/v1/mutes` returning accounts with an additional `mute_expires_at` attribute. We could do something similar, or return a new entity type in some `/api/v2/follow_requests`.
I'm new to this project and want to contribute. Can I work on this issue?
Yes, although I'm not sure what the most appropriate API would be. I personally would be fine with either of my two suggestions above, but other people (e.g. Gargron) may have another view on this.

review_comments:
Does this necessarily find the correct record?

At the controller level there's a query which makes sure that the accounts which are serialized are the accounts where the `current_account` (signed in user) is the target of the request ... but I think in this serializer the way this finder is now it would just find the first follow request where the account being serialized is the requester, which would not necessarily be the one relevant to current_account ... ?

We may need to pass in the current_account to serializer in order to confidently get the correct one.
Similar feedback here as in controller - make sure it's the one actually relevant to account requesting the endpoint.
